html:
The first Christian service held in New Zealand, preached by Samuel Marsden at Oihi Bay in the Bay of Islands on Christmas Day 1814.

Marsden was the senior Anglican chaplain of New South Wales, known there as a harsh magistrate and a sheep farmer. He had met Māori visitors in Sydney, among them the chief Ruatara, and planned a mission with the Church Missionary Society. Ruatara offered land and protection near his village of Rangihoua. Marsden sailed over with three lay missionaries and their families. On Christmas Day he preached to a crowd of Māori on the text "Behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy", and Ruatara explained the words to them.

The mission made few converts for years. Missionaries traded goods, including muskets, and the guns fuelled the Musket Wars between tribes. But mission schools spread reading and writing in Māori, and by the 1830s many Māori had become Christian. Missionaries later helped translate and promote the Treaty of Waitangi.
sum: The first Christian service held in New Zealand, preached by Samuel Marsden at Oihi Bay in the Bay of Islands on Christmas Day 1814.
